root_idea.summary: A thin, extended line or strand; the root centers on extension in narrowness and extends metaphorically to joined, linear, or upright forms.
root_idea.development: The basic image is the thread or fine strand. From it develop sewing, streaks resembling threads, dawn and night likened to contrasting threads, grouped things conceived as joined, and certain long or linear bodily forms.

senses.definition: A thread or string, serving as the image in the Quranic expression of the white thread and the black thread.
senses.usage_conditions: The literal thread-image underlies the contrasting expression in 2:187; the contextual interpretation of the two threads is given in the following sense.

senses.definition: In the Quranic paired expression “the white thread” and “the black thread,” the daylight or true dawn distinguished from the darkness or night.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a figurative construction based on the thin visible line or distinction between dawn and night, not a reference to sewing thread in context.
In the Quranic construction سَمِّ الْخِيَاطِ, it denotes the needle whose eye is being entered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sew, sew together, or sew up a garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I verb; the related noun خِيَاطَةٌ denotes the art or activity of sewing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To couple one camel with another by tying one animal’s halter to the other’s tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized use of the Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a serpent, to run or creep along the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage applied to the movement of a serpent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass by or along quickly; to journey on without stopping, including toward a destination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related form اِخْتَاطَ is also mentioned with this usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A needle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A classical meaning distinct from the Quranic خِيَاطٌ; it may occur alongside the ordinary meaning “thread.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: The spinal cord of the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical expression formed with خَيْطٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the idiom جَاحَشَ عَنْ خَيْطِ رَقَبَتِهِ, to defend one’s blood or life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension of the expression خَيْطُ الرَّقَبَةِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gossamer, fine scattered particles, or a faint shaft of light or matter visible through an opening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression has variant explanations, including gossamer, light entering a dark place, and scattered particles visible in sunbeams.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a proverb, something or someone of extremely little estimation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiomatic use based on the extreme fineness or insubstantiality of خَيْطُ بَاطِلٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A flock or collective group, especially of ostriches; also a swarm of locusts and, sometimes, a group of wild cattle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective sense is associated with things conceived as joined or gathered together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a plural-form usage; the same plural forms can also denote groups of animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The long neck or neck-bones of an ostrich; also a continuous black-and-white mixture or line in them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The linear or streak-like appearance motivates the specialized description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the dialect of Hudhayl, a wooden peg or stake fixed in a mountain for lowering oneself to a honey deposit; also a rope, slender rope, or tether-string used in honey gathering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources report several closely related identifications for the honey-gathering equipment, including peg, rope, and string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather tunic worn by a honey gatherer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized regional usage reported alongside the rope-and-peg meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا آتِيكَ إِلَّا الْخَيْطَةَ, an occasional or infrequent visit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning occurs in a fixed idiomatic construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female ostrich with a long neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective and noun describe the ostrich’s conspicuously extended neck.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To streak or mark with whiteness in thread-like lines, especially when gray hair appears on the head or beard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related reflexive construction describes a head becoming streaked with gray; the expression may also emphasize the joining or continuity of the white streaks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The art or activity of sewing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun associated with خَاطَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A seamster, one whose occupation is sewing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ordinary occupational noun formed from sewing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who passes along quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate, figurative noun use, not the occupational meaning “seamster.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment or piece of cloth that has been sewn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial noun describing a sewn article.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The whole of the exterior of the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of passage, especially the path along which a serpent creeps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is reported as disputed or incorrectly assigned by some authorities, but is explicitly recorded as a lexical interpretation.

cautions: Lane’s Quran citations use historical citation conventions; the modern example locations here follow the independently supplied QAC locations, especially 2:187 and 7:40.
The specialized خَيْطَةٌ and مَخِيطٌ meanings include competing or disputed interpretations, which are retained in their usage conditions rather than treated as certain ordinary senses.
